sources.title: Revisiting the low-volatility anomaly in cryptocurrency markets
sources.exact_claim_used: A low-volatility anomaly is present in cryptocurrency markets: high-volatility coins underperform low-volatility coins cross-sectionally on a risk-adjusted basis (spot-traded assets, recent sample).
sources.claim_scope_caveat: Evidence established on SPOT markets; perpetual transfer must re-earn the claim through funding, shorting and basis differences. Publication is a prior, never proof the repo implementation is profitable.

sources.title: Speculation and lottery-like demand in cryptocurrency markets
sources.venue: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money (Elsevier), vol. 71, art. 101289
sources.exact_claim_used: Cryptocurrency markets exhibit lottery-like demand: low-MAX (low recent extreme-positive-return) coins earn higher average raw and risk-adjusted returns than high-MAX coins; quintile spreads exceed ~1.5%/week.
sources.claim_scope_caveat: Spot sample predates 2021; lottery demand regimes may decay after publication; effect must survive perpetual funding costs and short-side feasibility.

sources.title: Lottery-like preferences and the MAX effect in the cryptocurrency market
sources.exact_claim_used: Extreme positive returns (MAX) are negatively priced cross-sectionally in crypto: highest-MAX deciles earn lower raw and risk-adjusted returns (reported spread 3.03% vs 1.99% between extreme deciles).
sources.claim_scope_caveat: Same spot-sample caveats as S2; MAX is tail-sensitive — the repo must show the effect is not one-fold concentration.

sources.title: Binance USD-M Futures market data endpoints (klines, funding rate history, open interest, mark price)
sources.exact_claim_used: Official semantics for completed 15m base bars, funding settlement timestamps (8h cadence), open-interest snapshots and mark price used for PIT feature construction and cost accounting in the frozen repo snapshot.
sources.claim_scope_caveat: Documentation describes current API; the frozen repo staging is the only admissible data source; no new external fetch without owner scope.
